title: River of Stars, River of Sand
caption: A dry riverbed under the Milky Way near Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A dry riverbed runs through the foreground while the Milky Way streams across the sky above it. ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek took the picture near ESO's Paranal Observatory in the Atacama Desert, which ranks among the driest places on Earth.

The photograph plays on two kinds of river. On the ground, the channel carved by long-gone water is empty. Overhead, the band of our galaxy looks like a flowing stream of light. One has dried up, while the other, as ESO puts it, keeps delivering new discoveries about the cosmos.

That dryness is part of why ESO built here. Dry air generally means clearer skies, which is what sensitive telescopes need. On these arid plains, ESO has designed and built what it describes as the most productive observatory in the world.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera near Paranal. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed here than it would to a person standing in the riverbed.

explore: The Milky Way appears as a band because we view our galaxy's flat disc from inside it, so the light of many distant stars merges into a continuous glow broken by dark dust.
alt: A dry riverbed in the desert beneath the Milky Way stretched across the night sky.
